MARKET.head: Pembrokeshire's Velfrey wins first Welsh trophy at Glass of Bubbly Awards
MARKET.summ: Pembrokeshire vineyard wins prestigious Glass of Bubbly trophy and gold medal, plus two silvers, competing against Champagne and sparkling wines from around the world. A family-run vineyard in Pembrokeshire has made Welsh wine history by winning a gold medal and a coveted category trophy at the prestigious international Glass...
takeaways: Velfrey Vineyard's Cuvée Reserve 2022 won gold and the Winter Warmer Trophy at the 2026 Glass of Bubbly Awards.
It is the first Welsh wine ever to win a trophy at the London-based competition, which judges only Champagne and sparkling wine.
Velfrey's Rhosyn 2023 and NV sparkling each took silver, giving the Pembrokeshire family vineyard medals for all three entries.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux leads fine wine trade as Lynch-Bages 2005 tops sales
MARKET.summ: US and UK buyers both upped their purchasing, the former segment reclaiming their share of purchasing
takeaways: Bordeaux held the lead in fine wine trade with a 37.4% share of purchases, with Lynch-Bages the top-traded wine overall.
Burgundy's share fell to 15.4% from 18.4% last week, below a September average of 24.6%.
US buyers rose to a 9.6% share of trade from 7.0% last week, and claimed over half of Bordeaux's purchased value.

MARKET.head: Surrey funds 17 rural projects, including a vineyard bird-repelling laser
MARKET.summ: A wine producer using bird-repelling lasers and cattle farmer using GPS collars to track livestock are among 17 innovative projects funded from a £500,000 pot to boost Surrey’s rural economy. Surrey County Council’s Farming Innovation Accelerator supports farmers and growers with funding for projects to modernise operations,...
takeaways: Surrey County Council's Farming Innovation Accelerator is funding 17 rural and farming projects from a £500,000 pot.
Each recipient receives a grant of up to £35,000 plus bespoke expert support, from over 50 proposals.
Albury Vineyard will install an automated bird-repellent laser protecting 18 acres of grapevines, adding over 1,700 bottles yearly.

MARKET.head: Australian wine exports fall 7% to $2.25bn as Canada and Southeast Asia offset US slump
MARKET.summ:
Australian wine exports declined overall in the year ending September 2026, but the results varied significantly across markets. Strong growth in Southeast Asia and Canada was offset by more challenging conditions in the United States (US). 

This Market Bulletin will analyse the latest export data, released...
takeaways: Australian wine export value fell 7 per cent to $2.25 billion, and volume fell 5 per cent to 590 million litres in the year to September 2026.
Exports to the US fell 28 per cent in value to $219 million, driven by a broader US wine market decline and import tariffs.
Southeast Asia grew 16 per cent in value to $291 million, with Thailand up 57 per cent, while Canada rose 12 per cent to $185 million.

MARKET.head: VinePair weekly roundup covers Supreme Court case, Uncle Nearest sale, and product releases
MARKET.summ: This is VinePair’s Booze News Weekly Roundup, where we gather the hottest headlines and product releases every Friday for a snapshot of what’s happening in the beverage alcohol industry. This week, we have updates on Diageo’s toxic chemical spill, SCOTUS to review a home distilling case, the latest product releases, and more.
takeaways: The Supreme Court will review a home distilling case, according to the weekly roundup.
Uncle Nearest's potential buyers and a Fawn Weaver motion to block the sale are covered.
Diageo's toxic chemical spill and Southern Glazer's bribery snafu are also reported in the roundup.

CULTURE.head: Navarra turns costly rosado methods into a premium identity; English wine could follow
CULTURE.summ: How Navarra Rosado turned production challenges into premium positioning and a compelling marketing story. Andrea Ontiveros Flores, a sommelier and marketing & communications specialist from Alicante, Spain asks if English wine could do the same? Consumers rarely pay more simply because winemaking is difficult.
takeaways: Navarra rosado producers use the Saignée method, requiring up to three times more grapes than standard red production, to signal premium intent.
Navarra's new Rosado Tradition designation requires Saignée and exclusive Garnacha, reinforcing the region's premium positioning.

CULTURE.head: Real Housewives' wine choices favor sweet, mass-market bottles over collectibles
CULTURE.summ: What do the reality stars’ drinking habits reveal about wealth, taste, status and the economics of the U.S. wine industry?
takeaways: Essayist Cake Zine contributor watched Real Housewives of Salt Lake City, noting Whitney Rose recommending Justin Cabernet, a $22 Walgreens bottle.
Housewives across franchises mostly drink mass-market, high-alcohol, high-sugar California cabernet sauvignon, often sweet.
Essay links this sweetness to critic Robert Parker's influence and the 100-point scoring system that shaped American wine taste.

SCIENCE.head: English vines hit by 2026 heatwaves, harvest 10-14 days early
SCIENCE.summ: With harvest complete, or nearing completion on many vineyards, Hutchinsons agronomists Rob Saunders and Will Robinson look at the impact of the record-breaking summer and what we can learn for future seasons. While 2026 could be remembered as a vintage season for some growers, others will look back less fondly, having first...
takeaways: Heatwaves in 2026 pushed 54 Met Office stations past all-time daily maximum temperature records this summer.
Harvest in English vineyards came around 10-14 days earlier than normal, with many crops reaching phenolic ripeness.
Bacchus struggled with intense heat and UV, while Sauvignon Blanc reached high alcohol and ripeness.

SCIENCE.head: UK vineyards face early harvest and drought after 2026 frost and heat
SCIENCE.summ: After a run of dramatically different vintages, 2026 has given UK viticulture another season that challenged assumptions, but also demonstrated just how much English and Welsh vineyards can achieve. The 2026 growing season began with a series of extraordinary frost events, creating a challenging start before developing into a...
takeaways: The 2026 English and Welsh growing season began with severe frost, then turned warm, dry and rapidly ripening.
Harvest arrived several weeks early at some vineyards, with dry weather keeping disease pressure low.
Vineyard Magazine argues UK growers must build resilience yearly through soil health, water management and site-specific choices.

SCIENCE.head: Domaine Bousquet details organic, water-saving and lightweight-bottle practices in Mendoza
SCIENCE.summ: Domaine Bousquet continues to elevate Argentine wine through generations of dedication and innovation in organic wine practices. Earlier this year, Irma Remigio and her team warmly welcomed SWR’s Membership Manager, Ilva Fridenberga, to their winery. The winery, located at the foot of the Andes Mountains, is globally recognized...
takeaways: SWR Membership Manager Ilva Fridenberga visited Domaine Bousquet's Mendoza winery at the foot of the Andes in February.
The estate is trialling biodiversity and garden vineyard corridors, with harvest done from outside the vine rows in the former.
Domaine Bousquet switched to high-pressure hoses for cleaning harvest boxes, cutting water use, and is a Bottle Weight Accord signatory targeting still bottles under 420g.

SCIENCE.head: MODIS satellite data validated for mapping vineyard evapotranspiration across regions
SCIENCE.summ: In North-Eastern Italy water demand for vineyards irrigation is constantly increasing, but this conflicts with the high civil and industrial rates of water consumptions in the area, which is one of the most densely populated in Europe
takeaways: University of Padova researchers Gianni Fila, Franco Meggio and Andrea Pitacco developed a remote-sensing method for mapping vineyard water consumption.
They used MODIS satellite data and ground meteorological observations on a 25-hectare vineyard in north-eastern Italy, with an eddy-covariance tower installed.
Estimates matched four years of eddy-covariance measurements, suggesting MODIS can monitor vineyard evapotranspiration at regional scale.

SCIENCE.head: Grenache rootstocks and irrigation shape water use in NE Spain vineyard
SCIENCE.summ: Under the context of global change, any decrease in water use by crops is essential, because water is becoming a more and more scarce resource, especially in Mediterranean areas, where grapevines are grown
takeaways: A three-year study in NE Spain tested Grenache grafted onto three rootstocks, irrigated and non-irrigated.
Non-irrigated vines had higher water use efficiency, and rootstocks 110-R and 41-B beat 161-49C.
Stomatal conductance differences from irrigation persisted through the season, peaking at veraison.

SCIENCE.head: Italian researchers outline viticulture strategies for climate change and biodiversity
SCIENCE.summ: In the globalization conditions possible future scenarios, optimistic and pessimistic are supposed
takeaways: Pisa University researchers say climate change may extend viticulture to higher latitudes and altitudes, requiring more resilient grapevine genotypes.
Italian regions have launched projects to recover local grapevine varieties at risk of abandonment in the global market.
Trials on Latium varieties Malvasia del Lazio and Cesanese d'Affile, plus Cabernet Sauvignon, tested Cordon Spur of Conegliano training.

SCIENCE.head: Conegliano pruning trials on Lazio grape varieties test yield and quality
SCIENCE.summ: In this work the salient results of the viticultural and ecomomic researches earned out on interesting italic varieties of Latium (Malvasia of the Lazio and Cesanese d'Affile) and an international vsriety (Cabernet sauvignon), "Cordon Spur of Conegliano" (CSC) as growing system, will be exposed
takeaways: Researchers at Italy's CRA viticulture centre and several Lazio and Padua institutions trialled Conegliano growing systems on Malvasia, Cesanese d'Affile and Cabernet Sauvignon.
The trials compared Vertical Tridimensional Minimal Pruning of Conegliano with and without DMRC, a double reasoned maturation method.
The stated aim is raising gross saleable product while improving quality, typicality and originality, with the work noting limited water and climate-driven overcropping.

SCIENCE.head: Winter vineyard jobs and the tools growers use to ease them
SCIENCE.summ: As autumn turns to winter a list of jobs looms large in the calendar. The vines need pruning and the soil needs care and attention. To make these jobs less demanding and costly, different tools can be used.
takeaways: Winter vineyard work includes pruning, soil care and frost protection, which growers can ease with specialised tools.
Cordless battery secateurs and a tractor-mounted pre-pruner cut hand-pruning time and reduce pulling out of canes.
Mechanical sweepers gather canes into a row so a flail mower can mulch the prunings at the same time.

SCIENCE.head: Portuguese trial cuts Loureiro and Borraçal yields with Ethephon and thinning
SCIENCE.summ: Some years, climate conditions and biological events increment the fertility of vines, which can lead to over cropping and a decrease of wine quality
takeaways: A 2007 trial in Vinhos Verdes tested Ethephon, Prohexadione-calcium and manual bunch thinning on Loureiro and Borraçal vines.
Manual bunch thinning cut Borraçal yield about 41% against control, versus about 26% for white Loureiro.
Ethephon at berry buck-shot stage lifted Loureiro sugar and lowered acidity, while Borraçal gained no quality benefit.

SCIENCE.head: Vine balance explained: how growth and crop load shift through the season
SCIENCE.summ: Vine balance is a commonly used term in viticulture that expresses the concept of an appropriate balance of vegetative to reproductive growth of the vine
takeaways: Vine balance describes the equilibrium between a vine's vegetative growth and its reproductive growth, the fruit it bears.
A balanced vine ripens its crop, sets fruitful buds for the next year, and builds reserves, without excessive canopy management.
Standard indirect measures such as yield to pruning weight ratio do not capture how growth balances shift during the season.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A deeper look at underwater wine aging
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Is a wine from the depths ‘better’ or does it depend on the boat?
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Attis, a winery owned by the Fariña family in O Grove, Galicia, ages its Albariño 'Mar' underwater in the Galician estuary.
The 2025 Attis Albariño 'Mar' is aged five months underwater at 13-16C, while the 'Standard' version of the same wine is not.
Attis produces about 120,000 bottles of its Standard Albariño annually, and the bottles aged underwater are magnums sealed with glass caps rather than cork.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What to Know Before This Year’s Hospices de Beaune Wine Auction
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover the world's most famous charity wine auction held since 1859. Get essential tips and insights for this year's legendary Burgundy event
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 166th Hospices de Beaune wine sale takes place Sunday 15 November 2026, with the first lot due around 2.30pm under the Halles de Beaune.
Last year's sale raised €18.8 million, with reds averaging €27,480 a cask and whites €58,580, and the Pièce de Charité fetched €400,000.

NEWSLETTERS.head: With these twelve wines, Juampi Michellini, Matias Riccitelli, Rafael Urreloja and Derek Mossman Knapp illustrate Argentina and Chile’s precocious ability to express the best in any variety
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Twelve wines, selected by their maker, four from Zorzal and four from Riccitelli, Undurraga and The Garage Wines Company, were
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Riccitelli's Patagonia Bastardo (Trousseau) is 100% from a vineyard planted in the 1970s, whole-bunch fermented and pressed to foudres, scoring 94/100.
Zorzal's Chardonnay Parcelario 2024 from Uco Valley, grown on a limestone-influenced block, received 95/100 from reviewer JG.
Urrejola's Undurraga Terroir Hunter Pinot Noir Trama 2022 comes from limestone in San Antonio Valley, five kilometres from the ocean, scoring 94/100.

NEWSLETTERS.head: S.O.R.B.E.T Wine Tasting: Nov 8, San Francisco
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I don’t know about you, but I love me a good acronym. S.O.R.B.E.T stands for Sonoma Organic Regenerative Biodynamic Educational
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow
takeaways: S.O.R.B.E.T is a wine tasting event scheduled for November 8 in San Francisco.
The acronym stands for Sonoma Organic Regenerative Biodynamic Educational.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Owendee
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The rituals of service for the holidays, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Wine-related search queries slump in July but rise sharply through October, peaking on December 31 before falling after New Year.
The October-to-December wine surge coincides with the Northern Hemisphere harvest, marking the wheel of the year.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Visiting the Vineyard in the Sky
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The extraordinary story of Domaine de Beudon in Valais, Switzerland
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Domaine de Beudon, at 890 metres in Valais, Switzerland, is run by the Granges-Faiss family, who have farmed there for over 50 years.
Jacky Granges-Faiss bought the estate in 1971 and became Valais's first Demeter certified estate in 1992, with his wife Marion, after his death in 2016.
Beudon's wines are fermented on the mountain but aged and bottled at Pierre-Antoine Crettenand's winery in Saillon, and use only sulphites as an additive since 2003.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Nasty Not Nice
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Why are people drinking less, when wine is better than ever? I have an idea. Wine is too good.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine is declining because the trade is too nice, and that wine should be made more complicated and insecurity-inducing.
He cites the Victorian cutlery and Riedel glass examples as models for making wine feel exclusive and intimidating to ordinary drinkers.
Atkin proposes ideas like separate barrel bottling and a Smithfield-style Primeur sale, arguing that excitement and risk should return to buying wine.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Inside Chinon’s Lieux-Dits Project
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Vignerons lead a collective effort to recognize the vineyards behind the appellation’s Cabernet Francs
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Chinon's lieux-dits project, begun by the Chinon Syndicat in 2014, aims to promote vineyard sites collectively without a formal classification.
Seven lieux-dits have been officially recognized so far, starting with La Croix Boissée in Cravant-les-Côteaux in 2018.
Each recognized site gets an in-depth monograph and an engraved stone marking the vineyard, with Matthieu Baudry of Domaine Bernard Baudry on the working group.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Yet Another Vintage Port Flex Post (Tasting Selections From 1985 - 2022)
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Last week, I published a bunch of reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the (stellar) 2024 Port vintage. I typically follow those type of posts up with another post of other, older selections of vintage Ports that I tasted at the same event, and I offer them without much shame as simply […] This article was...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude published reviews from an NYC media tasting of selections from the 2024 Port vintage.
A follow-up post covers older vintage Ports tasted at the same event, spanning 1985 to 2022.

NEWSLETTERS.head: 400 Montepulciano Bottles for Thomas Jefferson circa 1805
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine everyone’s been gushing over since the middle ages!
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: A trade contract dated October 17, 1350 between the Del Pecora family and merchant Jacopo di Vanni of Santa Fiora is the oldest known document for Vino Nobile di Montepulciano.
A 2024 document from the Jesuit archives in Montepulciano showed the term Vino Nobile was first used in 1766, replacing the previously assumed 1787 date.
In November 1805 Thomas Jefferson received 473 bottles of Montepulciano and later requested 400 bottles annually, specifying they come from ancient Jesuit vineyards.
